fatal_errors: The cited evidence supports rapid-quench amorphization of the undoped P20 alloy but provides no evidence that boron addition improves glass formation or thermal stability.
The proposed strong P–B bonding mechanism is asserted without structural, thermodynamic, spectroscopic, or computational support and is not established by the cited papers.
The intervention is compositionally underdefined because it does not identify which transition-metal component is replaced or give a normalized final alloy composition.
Testing only one melt-spinning condition does not adequately test improved glass-forming ability; both alloys may already be fully amorphous at that cooling rate.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the requested property goals and uses a sensible matched baseline, but it does not reconstruct the target intervention, which was redistribution of Fe/Co/Mn together with reduction of P to 15 at.% and comparison of slower arc solidification with 40 m/s melt spinning. Its mechanism and predicted compositional effects therefore disagree with the target. The proposed paired DSC/XRD/TEM experiment could test thermal stability, although a cooling-rate or ribbon-thickness series is needed to discriminate glass-forming ability. Boron-sensitive EDS is also technically challenging, especially at about 2 at.%. Most importantly, all cited evidence concerns the undoped alloy and rapid cooling; none validates boron alloying or P–B network formation. Thus the proposal is novel and superficially plausible but insufficiently evidence-supported.
